title: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting - Cultural and Creative Arts - Tie and Dye
exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: The fabric design technique where certain areas of a cloth are restricted from absorbing color by binding them tightly is known as:
questions.explain: Tie and Dye is a resist-dyeing technique in which portions of the fabric are tied securely to prevent dye from reaching those areas, thereby creating distinct patterns.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In the preparation of a dye bath, what is the primary function of Caustic soda and Hydrosulphite (Hydrochloride)?
options: To clean dirt off the fabric before dyeing.
To assist in the dissolving, penetrating, and fixing of dye onto the fabric.
To prevent the dye from touching the tied portions of the cloth.
To give the dyed fabric an appealing scent.
questions.explain: Chemicals like caustic soda and sodium hydrosulphite act as reducing agents and mordants; they reduce the dye into a soluble form so it penetrates the fabric and helps the dye bond (fix) permanently.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an accepted method for creating resist patterns in Tie and Dye?
questions.explain: Tying, folding, and stitching (tritik) are standard ways to bind fabric for dye-resistance. Smearing applies color directly rather than acting as a resist.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the name given to the mixture of hot water, dye pigments, and chemicals ready for immersing the fabric?
questions.explain: A 'dye bath' is the prepared liquid solution in a container (often a plastic bowl) into which the fabric is submerged for coloring.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Why must hand gloves be worn during the tie and dye process?
options: To improve the grip on wet fabrics.
To protect the hands from chemical burns and stubborn dye stains.
To add aesthetic value to the process of crafting.
To ensure the dye absorbs faster into the fabric.
questions.explain: Tie and dye involves harsh chemicals like caustic soda which can irritate or burn the skin, and strong dye pigments that stain the hands, hence the need for protective gloves.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: During the tie and dye process, what is the role of the wooden stick?
options: To stretch the fabric while drying.
To stir the dye bath and safely submerge the fabric into the hot chemicals.
To beat the fabric into softness after dyeing.
questions.explain: A long wooden stick is used as a tool to safely mix the dye solution and turn the fabric while it is soaking, keeping the artisan's hands away from the corrosive chemicals.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: After removing the fabric from the dye bath, what must be done to prevent the dye colors from bleeding excessively into the white resisted areas?
options: Immediately spread it in direct harsh sunlight.
Iron it while it is still tied.
Rinse the fabric properly in clean water before loosening the ties.
Apply soap to the dye bath before removing the fabric.
questions.explain: Rinsing removes the excess unfixed dye from the surface of the fabric so that when the strings are cut and the fabric is loosened, the white resist areas are not accidentally stained.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: The method of creating patterns in Tie and Dye by sewing the fabric tightly with needle and thread before dyeing is called:
questions.explain: Stitching (also known as Tritik) is a tie and dye method where a needle and thread are used to sew patterns onto the fabric. The thread is pulled tight to resist the dye in those stitched areas.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following is commonly used as a binding material to resist dye from penetrating certain parts of the fabric during the tying process?
questions.explain: Raffia, twine, and synthetic strings are commonly wrapped tightly around folded or gathered sections of the fabric to create a strong resist against the dye solution.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of folding the fabric before tying it in the tie and dye process?
options: To make the fabric dry faster after dyeing.
To save the amount of dye used in the bath.
To create symmetrical and rhythmic repeat patterns on the fabric.
To ensure the fabric fits into the plastic bowl easily.
questions.explain: Folding fabric in specific ways (such as pleating or square folds) before tying ensures that the resulting resist patterns are symmetrical and repeat evenly across the material.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Crafts, Media & Painting
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
